evidence_type.extraction: a verbatim quote located in a crawled document
evidence_type.falsification: a web passage found while trying to disprove the item (never verified)
evidence_type.human: provided or approved by a person

origin.DERIVED: concluded from other items (derived_from chain); no verbatim quote of its own
origin.DIRECT: stated verbatim by a source (evidence quotes it) or entered by a person
origin.EXPERIMENTALLY_VALIDATED: DIRECT and passed every applicable domain validator
origin.SYNTHESIZED: combined from several items (derived_from chain); no verbatim quote of its own

polarity.negative: what does not work or must be avoided (limitation, warning, anti-pattern)

provenance.DERIVED: no source of its own; follows the items it was derived from
provenance.OFFICIAL: the class of the most authoritative source is official (vendor / standards body)
provenance.ORGANIZATION: entered by a person as an internal standard or policy
provenance.USER: entered by a person as their own knowledge

relation_type.depends_on: the item relies on the target; a change there flags it for revalidation
relation_type.derived_from: the item was concluded or synthesized from the target

review_kind.falsification: counter-evidence found on the web; awaiting a reviewer
review_kind.manual: a person asked for a review
review_kind.quality: a quality rule flagged the item

status.CONFLICTED: an unresolved contradiction with another item exists
status.STALE: its evidence no longer appears in the current version of the source
status.SUPERSEDED: replaced by a newer item (historical: true); kept for provenance
status.SUPPORTED: at least one verified evidence record
status.VERIFIED: verification level >= 2: authoritative source and/or independent agreement

usage.caution: flagged for review, awaiting revalidation, CONFLICTED/STALE or carrying contradicting evidence; surface only with a warning (caution_reasons says why)
usage.cite: an ordinary current item: safe to answer with, citing it
usage.historical: superseded; do not answer with it

versioning_policy.major: renames/removes fields or files, or changes serialisation, hashing or the meaning of a value
versioning_policy.minor: adds optional fields, files or vocabulary values; consumers of the same major keep working
